summary: @apexacc/cli disables Windows Smart App Control and adds a Defender exclusion via hidden elevated PowerShell before dropping a remote binary
details: On Windows 11, apex.cjs launches a hidden UAC-elevated PowerShell process (Start-Process powershell -Verb RunAs -WindowStyle Hidden -ArgumentList '-NoProfile -EncodedCommand <base64>') that runs Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '<user home>\.apex' to whitelist that directory from Microsoft Defender and writes HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState=0 to disable Smart App Control / Code Integrity enforcement. The same script then downloads an approximately 105MB opaque binary from https://github.com/apexaccs/copilot GitHub releases into that now-excluded directory (~\.apex\bin) and executes it. The tampering is undocumented in the README, uses a hidden window and encoded command to conceal its actions from the user, and covers the very directory where the fetched executable is staged, shielding it from both signature-reputation blocking and antivirus scanning. An unused bin/apex shim additionally references a different GitHub repository (Apex-Accelerator/apexcli) than the active entrypoint (apexaccs/copilot), muddying provenance of the downloaded binary.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
